name: History (BA)

rules.name: Narrative Text
rules.desc:
The B.A. in History requires (major overview):
Completion of 13 eligible courses (for a minimum of 63 units), including:

• 1 Sources & Methods (HISTORY 1S-99S); to be completed as early as possible in undergraduate career

• 1 “Doing History” (HISTORY 200x); ideally completed before the end of sophomore year

• 1 Writing in the Major (HISTORY 209S); to be completed before the end of junior year

• 2 200-level Colloquia (HISTORY 201-298)

• 2 pre-1700 History courses

• 4 courses in a concentration of the student’s choosing; concentrations can be geographic (e.g., Africa, the United States), chronological (e.g., ancient, early modern), or thematic. Thematic concentrations include:

• Global Affairs and International Relations

• Law and Public Policy

• Environment, Science, Medicine and Technology

• Economics and Political Economy

• Religion and Intellectual History

• Activism, Public History and Public Service

• Gender and Sexuality

• Race and Ethnicity

• Urban and Spatial History

• Self-designed, in close consultation with major advisor
Completion of a Capstone Experience, by pursuing one of the two following options:

• Honor’s Thesis, which requires

• HISTORY 299H Junior Honors Colloquium; to be completed junior year

• HISTORY 299A/B/C Senior Research; to be completed senior year

• Completion of a thesis with a grade of B+ or higher

• Capstone Project, which requires

• HISTORY 299CA, CB, etc. Capstone Course; to be completed in autumn or winter of senior year

• HISTORY 299CW Creative Capstone Workshop; to be completed in spring of senior year

• Completion and presentation of project at Capstone Showcase; to be completed spring of senior year

rules.name: Sources and Methods Seminar (HISTORY 1S-99S)
rules.notes: The Sources and Methods seminar should be taken as early as possible in a student’s course of study. Ideally, it should be taken before the Doing History course (below) and it must be taken before enrolling in HISTORY209S Research Seminar for Majors (below).

rules.name: Doing History Colloquium (HISTORY 200x)
rules.notes:
Students are strongly encouraged to satisfy their “Doing History” requirement before the end of their sophomore year.
Optional additional "Doing History" colloquia may count toward the 200-level undergraduate colloquium requirement (see below).

rules.name: 200-level Undergraduate Colloquia (HISTORY 201-298)
rules.notes: Must be taken for a minimum of three units.

rules.name: 13 Courses and 63 Units
rules.desc: Students must complete a minimum of 13 courses and 63 units in the major.

rules.name: Remaining courses in History (3-5 units each)
Petitioned history-related courses from other departments (at most 10 units)
GPA of 2.0 or higher in History courses
Concentration
rules.notes:
History majors must complete four courses in a geographic (e.g., Africa, the United States) chronological (e.g., ancient, early modern), or thematic concentration.
Thematic concentrations include, but are not limited to:

• Global Affairs and International Relations

• Law and Public Policy

• Environment, Science, Medicine and Technology

• Economics and Political Economy

• Religion and Intellectual History

• Activism, Public History and Public Service

• Gender and Sexuality

• Race and Ethnicity

• Urban and Spatial History

• Self-designed, in close consultation with major advisor
Students should select a concentration in consultation with their advisor. See the History Department website for suggested course coherence.

rules.name: Writing in the Major (WIM)
rules.notes:
This course may be taken in the junior or senior year, but not before completing the Sources and Methods seminar and Doing History colloquium. Students who wish to write an honors thesis are expected take HISTORY 209S Research Seminar for Majors in their junior year.
HISTORY 209S Research Seminar for Majors fulfills the WIM requirement only. It does not fulfill geographical requirements or small group course requirements.

rules.name: Capstone Experience
rules.desc: The History Department offers a range of options for students to complete the capstone requirement:

children.name: Honors Thesis
children.notes: Please note that the honors thesis does not contribute units toward the major, so students who choose to complete an honors thesis for the capstone requirement must take an additional course to reach the 13 course and 63 unit minimum.
children.desc: The Honors Thesis (See “Honors” below for more information.)

children.name: Capstone Course
children.desc: Students complete a capstone course in Autumn or Winter and then refine their projects in the 1-unit Creative Capstone Workshop in Spring Quarter.

children.name: Capstone Courses
children.desc: To be taken in Autumn or Winter Quarter.
children.notes: Other capstone course options will be added to this list as they become available.

children.name: Creative Capstone Workshop
children.desc: To be taken in Spring Quarter.
children.notes: Students must also present their project at the spring Creative Capstone Showcase.

children.name: Present the project at the spring Creative Capstone Showcase
Paper Revision or Expansion
children.notes:
A student who cannot take either course or course may petition to fulfill the capstone requirement by revising or expanding work previously done for a history course, either in consultation with the faculty member for whom the paper was originally written, or with a faculty advisor who will work as a team with the original faculty reader. Revision or expansion must constitute at least 20-25 pages of written work, or a re-conceptualized, non-paper equivalent as determined by the relevant faculty member(s).
Petitions to revise or expand work previously done for a history course must be submitted to the Director of Undergraduate Studies for review by the first day of the quarter in which the student intends to revise or expand previous work. Students whose petitions are approved must enroll in course to track completion as well as HISTORY 299CW. Students must also present their project at the spring Creative Capstone Showcase.
Please note that a paper revision or expansion does not contribute units toward the major, so students who choose to revise or expand a paper for the capstone requirement must take an additional course to reach the 13 course and 63 unit minimum.

rules.name: Honors (optional)
rules.desc:
To graduate with departmental honors in History, students must:

• Complete HISTORY 299H Junior Honors Colloquium in the junior year. Students studying abroad during the winter quarter of their junior year are granted an automatic exemption from this requirement. Other exemptions are subject to the discretion of the Director of Honors.

• Complete HISTORY209S by the end of their junior year. Under rare circumstances, an exemption may be granted by the Director of Honors.

• Maintain a GPA of at least 3.3 in overall university work and a 3.5 in the History major during the final five quarters of enrollment/thesis preparation or obtain the consent of the director of the Honors Program.

• No later than autumn quarter of the senior year, select both an Advisor and a Second Reader who meet the eligibility criteria set forth in the department’s Honors Program Handbook

• Submit a completed honors thesis by the spring quarter deadline that meets submission requirements and receives a grade of B+ or above.

• Participate in mandatory Honors Program activities throughout the senior year (including, but not limited to, writing workshops and the annual honors thesis presentations) as specified in the Honors Program Handbook.
HISTORY 299A Senior Research I, HISTORY 299B Senior Research II, HISTORY 299C Senior Research III do not fulfill any history major requirements other than honors, but the units count toward the 180 required for BA degree conferral.

rules.name: Honors GPA: 3.3 overall and 3.5 in the major
Honors thesis (B+ or above) and Honors Program activities

gpa: The student must maintain a grade point average (GPA) in History courses of 2.0 or higher.
grading: Courses counting toward the major must be taken for 3-5 units and a letter grade.
policies:
Advising: Completion of the major requires planning. History majors should plan to meet with their faculty advisors twice yearly, once in the Autumn and once in the Winter or Spring quarters. These meetings should occur within the first three weeks of the quarter, before the final study list deadline.
Course and Unit Requirements:

• Students must complete at least 13 courses and 63 units in the major.

• At least 11 courses must be taken from the Stanford Department of History and carry the HISTORY designation or, alternately, be courses that the Stanford History Department has officially cross-listed. Transfer students and those who study abroad may be granted exemptions from this requirement at the discretion of the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

• One HISTORY299S Undergraduate Directed Research and Writing taken for 3-5 units and for a letter grade may be applied toward the 13 courses required for the BA in History.
Petition Policy for Stanford Courses: A maximum of 10 units of history-related coursework taken outside of the department may be petitioned to count toward the major. Unless otherwise specified, all coursework requires a syllabus and petition form to be submitted to the History Department for review. Please see the History Department website for the relevant petition form. Transfer students and those who study abroad may be granted exemptions from this policy at the discretion of the Director of Undergraduate Studies. Transfer students should refer to the External Credit Policies for guidance regarding transferring coursework at their previous institution toward the Stanford degree.
transferPolicy:
Students who transfer to Stanford with sophomore status may petition for up to four courses taken outside of Stanford to count toward the History major.
Students who transfer to Stanford with junior status may petition for up to six courses taken outside of Stanford to count toward the major.
Please note that the following major requirements are not transferable:

• Sources & Methods Seminar

• Doing History Colloquium

• Research Seminar for Majors (History 209S)

• Capstone
Transfer students should refer to the External Credit Policies for guidance regarding transferring coursework at their previous institution toward the Stanford degree. Advanced Placement credits do not fulfill any major requirements.
otherRequirements: 2 from HISTORY201-298 (minimum of 3 units) plus 1 from HISTORY 200-series and 1 from HISTORY 1S-99S series (minimum of 5 units)
reviewNotes: The audit checks the 63 units and 13 courses, at least 11 of them HISTORY courses (cross-listings count), each taken for 3-5 units and a letter grade: a Sources and Methods seminar, a Doing History colloquium, two 200-level colloquia, two pre-1700 courses, HISTORY 209S (the WIM course) and a capstone, with other HISTORY courses filling the rest (one HISTORY 299S may count). Honors research courses do not count toward the major. Checked by hand: the four-course concentration you set with your advisor, the 2.0 GPA in History courses, up to 10 units of petitioned courses from other departments, the honors thesis or paper-revision capstone, which add no units, and presenting a capstone project at the spring Creative Capstone Showcase. AP credit does not count.
